blocks.text: Living in Northeast Maple Ridge

parts.t: Northeast Maple Ridge is an MLS® sub-area name. The City of Maple Ridge doesn’t publish a boundary for it. The City’s neighbourhood list names Albion/Kanaka, Port Hammond, Port Haney, Ruskin, Silver Valley, Thornhill, Town Centre, Webster’s Corners, Whonnock and Yennadon, with no northeast area.

As a rough guide only, I think of it as the east side of the city, east of 240 Street to the Mission boundary, from the Fraser River flats up to the forested land near Golden Ears Park, with Dewdney Trunk Road as the main east–west road. That is my reading, not a City boundary. It overlaps my

guides. The closest official descriptions are Webster’s Corners, which the City says is near the border of Maple Ridge and Mission, just off Dewdney Trunk Road, and the City’s North 256 Street Industrial Lands Area Plan, which covers lands in northeast Maple Ridge.

Written by Jared Gibbons, REALTOR®, Royal LePage Little Oak Realty, on October 17, 2026. I have worked in Lower Mainland real estate for 11+ years. Facts come from the official sources noted on this page. Rules and boundaries change, so confirm anything important with the City of Maple Ridge and School District 42.
Not legal, planning or financial advice. Confirm zoning, plan designations, flood rules and school catchments before you buy or sell.

blocks.text: Northeast Maple Ridge at a glance

parts.t: Gathered from official sources. Details change, so use the links on each card to double-check.

blocks.text: Buses on the east side Routes 701, 748 and 749

parts.t: Route 701 runs east from Haney Place along Dewdney Trunk Road to 250 Street, Smith Avenue and 248 Street (Maple Ridge East). Some weekday trips continue non-stop to Mission City Station

Route 748, Thornhill / Haney Place, is a loop from Haney Place via River Road, 240 Street, McClure Drive and Jackson Road to 100 Avenue, 256 Street, 98 Avenue, 264 Street and 268 Street, then back along 100 Avenue. Trips run about every two hours, and some go via Port Haney Station

Route 749, Ruskin / Haney Place, is a loop from Haney Place to 280 Street at Lougheed Highway and back. Going out it uses Dewdney Trunk Road, 284 Street and 116 Avenue, and coming back it uses Lougheed Highway, 272 Street and Dewdney Trunk Road

Timetable dates: 701, effective January 1, 2024; 748, effective April 20, 2026; 749, effective June 8, 2026. TransLink’s August 24, 2026 news post says service improvements on route 701 start September 7, 2026, so check the current timetable.

parts.t: Council adopted the Official Community Plan amendments on June 23, 2026
About 500 acres on both sides of 256 Street north of 128 Avenue, with existing uses that include gravel extraction, institutional operations and civic services

parts.t: The Official Community Plan holds Thornhill as a long-term Urban Reserve. Urban development will not be supported there until the City’s population exceeds 100,000 and the residential capacity within the existing urban area is approaching build-out
Until those conditions are met, the minimum parcel size for subdivision of land designated Urban Reserve is 2.0 hectares (about 4.9 acres)

blocks.text: City park Thornhill Park and Thornhill Trails

parts.t: Thornhill Park is at 26007 98 Avenue and has a tone pole disc golf course, a community hall, a playground and a tennis court
The City’s neighbourhoods page says the mountain biking and hiking trail network on 256 Street has 17 trails, rated moderately difficult and usually taking an hour to complete
Thornhill Trails is at 10390 256 Street. The City completed a 24-stall parking lot there in summer 2023

blocks.text: Metro Vancouver Kanaka Creek Regional Park

parts.t: 11450 256 Street, Maple Ridge (the address TransLink gives for the park)

items.t: 400 hectares of park along 12 kilometres of Kanaka Creek

parts.t: Canyon Trail runs from the fish hatchery to Cliff Falls, 1.2 km one way with some challenging hills. The flat Riverfront Trails are 3 km one way
Metro Vancouver says the cliffs at Cliff Falls are steep and slippery and asks visitors to stay out of the creek and canyon there

blocks.text: BC Parks Golden Ears Provincial Park

parts.t: The park is 11 km north of Maple Ridge. Drivers go along Dewdney Trunk Road, turn onto 232nd Street, then turn onto Fern Crescent at the traffic circle
Established in 1927 and named after the twin peaks of Mount Blanshard
A popular spot for swimming, windsurfing, water-skiing, canoeing, boating and fishing. Canoes and kayaks can be rented at the Alouette (South Beach) day-use area, weather permitting

The City says Webster’s Corners features a network of trails for mountain bikers in the BCIT Woodlot

blocks.text: Planning and flood notes for Northeast Maple Ridge

parts.t: Plans, zoning and flood rules can be different for each lot.
The North 256 Street Industrial Lands Area Plan covers about 500 acres on both sides of 256 Street north of 128 Avenue. Council adopted the Official Community Plan amendments on June 23, 2026.

The Official Community Plan holds Thornhill as a long-term Urban Reserve. Urban development will not be supported there until the City’s population exceeds 100,000 and the residential capacity within the existing urban area is approaching build-out.

Before urban development can happen in the Thornhill Urban Reserve, the OCP requires approval of an amended Regional Context Statement by the Metro Vancouver Board, approval of an extension to the Fraser Sewerage Area by the Greater Vancouver Sewerage and Drainage District Board, and an area plan adopted by Council.
Until those conditions are met, the minimum parcel size for subdivision of land designated Urban Reserve is 2.0 hectares (about 4.9 acres).
The City adopted updates to the Official Community Plan in November 2025.

ALR: I did not find an official statement placing Agricultural Land Reserve land inside Northeast Maple Ridge as a whole. ALR status is set parcel by parcel, so check the exact address on the Agricultural Land Commission map.
The City’s Official Community Plan includes policies to enhance and promote farming on lands designated in the Agricultural Land Reserve.
The City publishes a North and South Alouette River Floodplain Map and a Fraser River Floodplain Map, and says a floodplain map outlines the area expected to flood on average once every 200 years.
The City monitors rainfall and water levels in the Fraser River, the North and South Alouette River and Kanaka Creek.
The City says some parts of Maple Ridge face landslides and debris flows, and that melting snowpacks combined with warm weather can create landslides.
I found no flood or slope area named for Northeast Maple Ridge as a whole, so check the City’s maps for the exact address.

The City’s lot-size guide for rural designations is in the Official Community Plan, Chapter 3. Rural Residential lots are generally 0.8 hectares (about 2 acres) where community water is available and 2.0 hectares (about 4.9 acres) where water is on site.

Northeast Maple Ridge has no West Coast Express station. The West Coast Express has two Maple Ridge stops, Maple Meadows Station and Port Haney Station, with five trips daily, leaving Maple Ridge in the morning and returning in the evening, Monday to Friday.

blocks.text: Before you buy in Northeast Maple Ridge

parts.t: Check the Urban Reserve and the zone.
If the property is in Thornhill, ask the City what the Urban Reserve policy means for subdividing or building on that parcel.
Check the water, septic and access.
Ask who supplies the water, ask for well and septic records, and check how the property is reached in winter.
Check the ALR on larger lots.
Look up the address on the Agricultural Land Commission map before you plan anything on farmland.
Check the slope and flood maps.
Ask the City what the floodplain, creek and slope rules mean for the exact address.
Ask SD42 for the exact address.
Check the roof, drainage, furnace, plumbing and wiring, and have the well water tested if there is a well.
